Looking at the renders, I notice the phoenix body seems small relative to the wings, and the feathers look thin and sparse from the three-quarter angle, especially since they lie flat and edge-on from the front view. I'm considering widening the feathers to give the wings more visual presence.

The head reads clearly as a bird with a reasonable beak, crest, and visible eye, while the hunched body and short legs feel proportionate. Composition-wise, the subject fills the frame well from the front, though the pillar flames at certain angles (70° and 290°) sit close to the dais edge and could partially obstruct the view.

Now I'm noticing the pillars float just off the dais edge since the dais radius is smaller than the pillar placement radius, so I need to either enlarge the dais or pull the pillars inward so their bases sit properly on the dais surface rather than hovering at ground level. I'm working out a scaling factor to enlarge the dais profile and rune plane proportionally so everything lines up — dais radius near 1.7, rune circle around 1.25, and pillars pulled in to roughly 1.55 so their bases land on the dais top.

I'll settle on pillars at radius 1.47, deciding the current placement is close enough and the loose-part note is just informational rather than something to fix. Rather than fuss more over composition, I should look at other gains—checking the back view, the tail ribbons look thin and fan out low beneath the body, though the side view extension reads fine.

I want to widen the tail ribbons from 0.12 to 0.17 and thicken them since the tail is the key phoenix feature that needs to read as flowing rather than streaky. Similarly, the wing feathers look like narrow streaks in the three-quarter view, so I should thicken those too given the wingspan of 5.7m against a 0.7m body with roughly 0.9m wing chord—the sweep and shoulder attachment at y=1.12 rising to 1.55 at the tips look fine otherwise. I'm also noticing the body proportions feel too tiny relative to the wingspan, and the chest fluff looks scrubby rather than full.

For the chest coloring, I'm thinking the fur shading from red above to gold below is creating a muddy mustard tone, so brightening the belly to a lighter gold would help. I'll also scale up the body radii by about 1.2x to make the hero figure feel bigger, checking that this doesn't clip into the wing shoulder or hip attachment points—running the numbers, the shoulder and legs still clear fine with the enlarged body.

Looking at the legs and feet, they seem thin and the stance checks out, with toe spikes landing right around the dais height so nothing floats or clips through the floor. The eye decal looks too small for the enlarged head, so I want to bump its scale up by about 15%.

Now looking at the head close-up, I notice a dark spotted shape near the collar that looks off—like the chest emblem decal is bleeding up and stretching onto the neck area instead of staying on the torso where it belongs.

I'm planning some modest edits: enlarge the hero body and brighten the belly, widen the tail ribbons and feather spread, make wing feathers fuller by increasing their width without overlapping the core, enlarge the eye, and reposition the pillars closer to the dais while shifting the front ones to avoid blocking the view.
